result:
The proposed solution's second step is wrong, so its answer of 180 is not reliable.

The solution correctly notes that the counts must be exactly 0, 1, …, 2024, so one gnome must see nobody and another must see everyone.

The error is in the "clustered configuration" argument. It claims that no gnome can see nobody once α exceeds about 0.178°. That is false, because any gnome on the convex hull has an empty angular gap greater than 180° outside the hull. Since α < 180°, a hull gnome can always be turned to see nobody. So count 0 is never the obstruction, and the clustered configuration does not rule out any α.

The real constraint comes from count 2024, which requires some gnome to see all the others. The regular 2025-gon is a plausible worst case, and there α ≥ 180·2023/2025 ≈ 179.82° is needed. This suggests S is a nonempty interval of values close to 180 (possibly with other constraints), not the empty set. I did not work out S exactly.

If S is nonempty and its values approach 180, then sup S = 180 and inf S is positive. The sum would then be well above 180 (around 360 if inf S is near 179.82), not 180. The answer 180 came only from the wrongly derived S = ∅ with the convention inf ∅ = 180 and sup ∅ = 0.

VERDICT: REJECT
